name: Sustanon (testosterone blend)

lead: Sustanon is the brand name of mixed-ester testosterone injections. Sustanon 250 combines four testosterone esters (propionate, phenylpropionate, isocaproate and decanoate), and Sustanon 100 combines three of them (propionate, phenylpropionate and isocaproate).
The blend is intended to give a mix of faster and slower release. Little published research is available in the sources reviewed for this wiki, and none examines appearance outcomes.

paras: Each ester is a prodrug that is cleaved to release testosterone after intramuscular injection; shorter esters act sooner and longer ones last longer, so a blend spreads release over time.

As with other testosterone products, general risks include acne, sperm suppression, raised red blood cell counts and cardiovascular and prostate considerations. Testosterone is a controlled substance in many countries.

lead: Sustanon is the brand name for blended testosterone ester injectables. Sustanon 250 contains four esters (propionate, phenylpropionate, isocaproate and decanoate), while Sustanon 100 contains three (propionate, phenylpropionate and isocaproate) [1].

Testosterone esters generally are prodrugs that are converted to testosterone in the body, and injection of esters in oil is the most common route for testosterone replacement [2]. The sources available for this entry do not detail Sustanon's manufacturer history or trial data, so this article is brief.

paras: The two Sustanon products differ by whether the long-acting decanoate ester is included [1]. Common injectable testosterone esters, including propionate and decanoate relatives such as cypionate and enanthate, act as prodrugs [2].

General testosterone-therapy effects include acne, oily skin and hair loss, suppression of sperm production, and warnings about cardiovascular events, prostate conditions and blood pressure; testosterone is contraindicated in pregnancy [2]. Injectable oil preparations can cause pulmonary oil microembolism, with cough and shortness of breath [2].
